5_1.headline: Write down who works for you
5_1.teaser: A list of your suppliers and service providers.
missed: It is not only IT firms that count. It covers every direct supplier and service provider that touches your IT or your data, including for example the tax adviser with access to staff data (§ 30(1) and (2) no. 4 BSIG).

learn.title: Who works for your company
body: The security of your IT also covers whoever works on it from outside or can reach your data: service providers, software vendors, suppliers. The law calls them your direct suppliers and service providers. The first step is a list of who they are and what they do for you.
Start with the ones your business could not run without. The list grows over time.
learn.duty: The law requires measures for supply chain security, including in your relationships with your direct suppliers and service providers.

list.title: What your list can look like
list.caption: One line per supplier, with what they do for you. These are the usual kinds:

rows.name: IT service provider
rows.detail: looks after servers, accounts and backups, has remote access

rows.name: Software and cloud providers
rows.detail: for example Microsoft for email and files, DATEV for the books

rows.name: Web agency or host
rows.detail: runs the website or the webshop

rows.name: Machine or equipment maintenance
rows.detail: services machines and connects remotely for diagnostics

rows.name: Building and security services
rows.detail: alarm system, access cards, cleaning with keys

rows.name: Logistics and couriers
rows.detail: ship to your customers, see order and address data

ready.title: For the next step: your list of creditors
ready.lead: Almost everyone who works for you sends you invoices. So the quickest start is the list from your accounting.

items.name: List of creditors
items.detail: your bookkeeping can export it, for example from DATEV or your accounting software, or your tax adviser sends it; the last twelve months are enough

items.name: Contracts and subscriptions
items.detail: what you pay by card or direct debit: maintenance contracts, software licences, cloud accounts

items.name: Your IT service provider
items.detail: knows which vendors it uses on your behalf

ready.source: Building on overviews that already exist is how the BSI advises compiling any inventory (BSI-Standard 200-2).
ready.confirm: I have the list of creditors at hand

suppliers.title: Your suppliers
suppliers.lead: Whoever you named as the provider of your software and technology is already on it. Add the others, one line each with what they do for you. When in doubt, write it down rather than leave it out.

done.title: Your list is in place
done.note: When a new supplier comes along, add it to the list.
